releases.name: oc-media v0.1.2
releases.body:
Security fix: **session isolation for the raw-body media stash** (potential cross-session media disclosure).

The shared in-memory `MediaStash` keyed entries only by note text (name/mime/size), while injection matched attachment descriptions without verifying ownership — so a request originating from one OpenCode session could potentially splice in media bytes stashed by another session carrying a matching description.

### What changed

- **Session ownership enforced.** Every stash entry records the session whose `read` captured it; the entry key binds the session ID (`sha256(sessionId + note)`) and every lookup — exact and contains-scan — re-verifies ownership. The `http.request` hook passes the dispatching session's ID, so an unrelated session's request injects nothing even with the exact note text in hand.
- **Unpredictable attachment IDs.** Each read mints a fresh 128-bit random token embedded in the tool-result note (`[media attached: … #<token>]`), replacing filename/description-based matching entirely — the same file read twice yields different notes, and a crafted description can't name an entry it didn't read.
- **Cache lifetime.** Entries are dropped when their session is deleted (along with its tracked model), and re-homed only along the `session.forked` parent → child lineage. Isolation itself never depends on event delivery — ownership is verified at injection regardless.
- **Isolation tests.** Two sessions with identical file names/sizes but different media bytes, byte-identical note text across sessions, forged exact-note injection attempts, session-scoped injection, deletion, and fork inheritance: cross-session retrieval never occurs.

Verification: full suite green (109 tests), `tsc --noEmit` clean.

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/oc-media

releases.name: oc-media v0.1.0
releases.body:
First release of **oc-media**.

An OpenCode V2 plugin that teaches the native `read` tool to ingest **audio** and **video** files — capability-driven from the models.dev catalog, never a hardcoded model list.

### Highlights
- **Capable models read audio/video directly** through `read`; incapable models get a clear tool error instead of a silent failure, and their Read description never over-claims.
- **Raw-body delivery** (`input_audio` / `video_url`) on OpenAI-Chat-shaped transports (OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, …) — the model genuinely hears and sees the media.
- **Automatic MKV/WebM → MP4 remux** on MP4-only transports: stream copy → audio transcode → full transcode cascade (FFmpeg required for remuxing).
- **Compress-first guidance** in the system prompt, tool description, and size error: oversize media is compressed with FFmpeg (fast preset) and read, instead of frame extraction.
- Fail-closed on unknown capability data (`allowUnknown` opt-in), bounded caches, and everything non-media stays byte-for-byte native.

### Install
```jsonc
// opencode.json(c)
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "oc-media" }]
}
```

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/oc-media
